extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, care provider facilities, potential sponsors, PRS providers, and legal representatives involved with unaccompanied children
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory standards governing placement, sponsor suitability, release procedures, home study requirements, appeals, and post-release services for unaccompanied children in ORR custody. Includes required notices, timelines, recordkeeping, and minimum standards for care provider facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of unaccompanied children and their children together
rubrics_metrics.description: If unaccompanied children and their children are referred together to ORR, ORR shall place the unaccompanied children and their children in the same facility, except in unusual or emergency situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unusual or emergency situations include (1) alternate placement due to hospitalization or need for specialized care the facility cannot provide; (2) the unaccompanied child requests alternate placement for their child; (3) the unaccompanied child is subject to allegations of abuse or neglect against their child or temporary urgent separation for the child's protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services for children of unaccompanied children
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR provides the same care and services to the children of unaccompanied children as it provides to unaccompanied children, as appropriate, regardless of the children's immigration or citizenship status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. citizen children of unaccompanied children are eligible for public benefits and services to the same extent as other U.S. citizens; care provider facilities shall submit applications on behalf of those children and exhaust those benefits before using ORR-funded services to the greatest extent practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required notice of legal rights to unaccompanied children
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall promptly provide each unaccompanied child in its custody, in a language and manner the child understands, with a State-by-State list of free legal service providers, a specified explanation of the right of potential review, and a presentation regarding their legal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explanation text is provided in the regulation; materials must be understandable in language and manner appropriate to the child. ORR shall not retaliate against legal service providers or representatives for advocacy or appearance adverse to ORR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Subpart C — release without unnecessary delay
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart covers the policies and procedures used to release, without unnecessary delay, an unaccompanied child from ORR custody to a vetted and approved sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of preference for sponsors for release
rubrics_metrics.description: When ORR determines release is appropriate, ORR shall release a minor without unnecessary delay in the following order of preference: (1) a parent; (2) a legal guardian; (3) an adult relative; (4) an adult individual or entity designated by the parent or guardian; (5) a standard program willing to accept legal custody; (6) an adult individual or entity seeking custody when no other alternative exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation can be via declaration signed under penalty of perjury before an immigration or consular officer or other document satisfactory to ORR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination of potential sponsors based on immigration status
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall not disqualify potential sponsors based solely on their immigration status and shall not collect information on immigration status of potential sponsors for law enforcement or immigration enforcement related purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR will not share any immigration status information relating to potential sponsors with law enforcement or immigration enforcement entities at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: No release on child's own recognizance
rubrics_metrics.description: In making determinations regarding release, ORR shall not release unaccompanied children on their own recognizance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor application package requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential sponsors shall complete an application package to be considered as a sponsor for an unaccompanied child; the package may be obtained from the care provider facility or ORR directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum components of sponsor suitability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to releasing a child, ORR shall conduct a suitability assessment that at minimum consists of review of the potential sponsor's application package, including verification of the sponsor's identity, physical environment of the sponsor's home, relationship to the child (if any), and an independent finding that the individual has not engaged in activity indicating potential risk to the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may consult with the issuing agency (e.g., consulate or embassy) to verify the validity of identity documentation presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional/Additional elements of sponsor assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may require investigation of living conditions, verification of employment/income, interviews with household members, a home visit or home study, background and criminal records checks (including fingerprint-based), and consideration of the child's wishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These components are part of the suitability assessment as needed and may be required in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of relationship to child and family
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall assess the nature and extent of the potential sponsor's previous and current relationship with the unaccompanied child, and the child's family, if applicable; ORR may deny release to unrelated individuals who have no pre-existing relationship with the child or family prior to ORR custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of sponsor motivation and preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall consider the potential sponsor's motivation for sponsorship and the unaccompanied child's and the child's parent's or legal guardian's preferences and perspectives regarding release to the potential sponsor, as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of unaccompanied child's functioning and risk factors
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall evaluate the child's current functioning and strengths in conjunction with risks or concerns such as: victim of sex or labor trafficking; history of criminal/juvenile justice involvement; history of behavioral issues; history of violence; individualized needs including disabilities or medical/mental health issues; history of substance use; parenting or pregnant status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should consider nature of criminal involvement (e.g., adjudicated, represented by counsel, type of offense).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of sponsor strengths/resources and risks (for individual sponsors)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall consider the potential sponsor's strengths and resources in conjunction with risks that could affect their ability to function as a sponsor including criminal background, substance use or history of abuse/neglect, physical environment of the home, and other child welfare concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor understanding and planning assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall assess the potential sponsor's understanding of the child's needs; plan to provide adequate care, supervision, and housing; understanding of responsibilities related to immigration court proceedings, school attendance, and U.S. child labor laws; and awareness of and ability to access community resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of a release plan with post-release services
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall develop a release plan that will enable a safe release to a potential sponsor through the provision of post-release services if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and continuous family unification efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR or the care provider shall make and record prompt and continuous efforts toward family unification and release, including intakes, admissions assessments, and ongoing case management services to identify potential sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of release requirements to child and sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: If a potential sponsor is identified, ORR shall explain to both the unaccompanied child and the potential sponsor the requirements and procedures for release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor Care Agreement obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The sponsor's application includes a Sponsor Care Agreement requiring the sponsor to: (1) provide for the child's physical and mental well-being; (2) ensure compliance with DHS and immigration courts' requirements; (3) adhere to federal and state child labor and truancy laws; (4) notify DHS, EOIR, and other relevant parties of address changes; (5) provide notice of initiation of dependency proceedings or any risk to the child; (6) for non-parents/guardians, notify ORR of a child moving to another location or change of address and notify ORR within 72 hours if temporarily transferring physical custody in emergency situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR refusal to release to persons/agencies with reasonable belief of harm or failure to present
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall not be required to release a child to any person or agency it has reason to believe may harm or neglect the child or fail to present the child before DHS or the immigration courts when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor education during release approval
rubrics_metrics.description: During the release approval process, ORR shall educate the sponsor about the needs of the unaccompanied child and develop an appropriate plan to care for the child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of home studies
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of assessing sponsor suitability, ORR may require a home study, which includes investigation of living conditions where the child would be placed, the standard of care the child would receive, and interviews with the potential sponsor and others in the household; it takes place prior to the child's physical release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances requiring home studies under TVPRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Home studies are required for: (i) a child who is a victim of a severe form of trafficking; (ii) a special needs child with a disability; (iii) a child victim of physical or sexual abuse indicating significant harm or threat; (iv) a child whose proposed sponsor clearly presents a risk of abuse/maltreatment/exploitation/trafficking based on all available objective evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References statutory authority: TVPRA at 8 U.S.C. 1232(c)(3)(B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Home study required for certain non-relative sponsors and young children
rubrics_metrics.description: Home studies are required before releasing any child to a non-relative sponsor who is seeking to sponsor multiple children or who previously sponsored a child and seeks to sponsor additional children; and before releasing any child 12 years old or younger to a non-relative sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR discretion to initiate home studies
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may, in its discretion, initiate home studies if it determines a home study is likely to provide additional information which could assist in determining that the potential sponsor is able to care for the child's health, safety, and well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care provider obligations relating to home studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The care provider must inform the potential sponsor whenever a home study is conducted, explain the scope and purpose, answer questions, and provide the home study report and any addendums to the potential sponsor if the release request is denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-release services for children with home studies
rubrics_metrics.description: An unaccompanied child for whom a home study is conducted shall receive post-release services as described at §410.1210.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for denial of potential sponsorship
rubrics_metrics.description: A potential sponsorship will be denied if ORR determines the potential sponsor is not capable of providing for the child's physical and mental well-being or that the placement would result in danger to the child or the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely adjudication of parent or legal guardian sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall adjudicate a potential sponsor who is an unaccompanied child's parent or legal guardian within 10 calendar days of receipt of a completed sponsor application or Family Reunification Package (FRP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements when denying release to parent/legal guardian
rubrics_metrics.description: If ORR denies release to a parent or legal guardian, it must notify the potential sponsor in writing via a Notification of Denial letter that includes: (1) explanation of reason(s); (2) evidence/information supporting denial; (3) instructions for requesting an appeal; (4) notice that additional evidence may be submitted before or during a hearing; (5) notice that the sponsor may present witnesses and cross-examine ORR's witnesses; (6) notice that the sponsor may be represented by counsel at no cost to the Federal Government in proceedings related to the denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR obligation to inform child and representatives of denial
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall inform the unaccompanied child, the child's child advocate, and the child's counsel (or local legal service provider if no attorney) of a denial of sponsorship involving a parent or legal guardian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special notice and appeal rights when sole reason is safety concern
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sole reason for denial is concern that the child is a danger to self or others and the potential sponsor is the child's parent or guardian, ORR must send the child a copy of the Notification of Denial, and the child may seek an appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to counsel for release and denial proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall permit unaccompanied children to have the assistance of counsel, at no cost to the Federal Government, with respect to release or the denial of release to a proposed sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process for denied parent/legal guardian sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: Denied parent or legal guardian sponsors may seek an appeal of ORR's decision by submitting a written request to the Assistant Secretary of ACF or designee; the requestor may seek an appeal with or without a hearing; the Assistant Secretary or designee will acknowledge the request within a reasonable time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child's right to appeal specific-denial safety determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sole reason for denial is concern the child is a danger to self or others, the child may seek appeal as described for sponsors; the child may consult with counsel and may seek appeal any time after denial while in ORR custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: 90-day review of pending sponsor applications
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR Federal staff supervising case management shall review all pending sponsor applications or FRPs for children in ORR custody 90 days after the complete sponsor application or FRP was submitted to identify and resolve reasons for pending status and determine steps to accelerate safe release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review updates and subsequent reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of the initial 90-day review, case managers shall update the sponsor and child on case status and work to address unresolved portions; for cases not resolved, additional reviews at least every 90 days until resolved, with discretion for more frequent reviews subject to resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility categories for Unaccompanied Refugee Minors (URM) Program
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may release a child to the URM Program; eligible categories include Cuban and Haitian entrants as defined by statute, victims of a severe form of trafficking, individuals classified as Special Immigrant Juveniles (with conditions), U nonimmigrant status recipients, and other populations as authorized by Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR will evaluate each case to determine whether referral to URM is in the child's best interests; legal custody/guardianship must be established under State law when discharging to URM and ORR retains custody until established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting specific consent for custody proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An unaccompanied child must request specific consent from ORR if the child seeks to invoke juvenile court jurisdiction to alter the child's custody status or release from ORR custody; attorneys must complete a request for specific consent prior to juvenile court determining or altering custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: if the juvenile court is invoked only to petition for SIJ classification or to permit court jurisdiction regarding placement but not to alter custody, specific consent is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement and decision timeframes for specific consent requests
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall acknowledge receipt of specific consent requests within two business days and make determinations within 60 business days; ORR shall expedite urgent requests when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR shall inform the child or the child's attorney/representative in writing of the decision and the evidence used to make it. Reconsideration of denial may be requested within 30 business days to the Assistant Secretary for ACF, who will send a final administrative decision within 15 business days of receipt of the reconsideration request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-release preparation obligations of care provider facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Before releasing children, care provider facilities shall work with sponsors and children to prepare for safe and timely release, assess need for community resources, and provide guidance regarding safety planning and accessing services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of Post-Release Services (PRS) after home study
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall conduct PRS, during the pendency of removal proceedings, for children for whom a home study was conducted; children who receive a home study and PRS may also receive home visits by a PRS provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may, at its discretion and subject to appropriations, conduct PRS in additional cases involving children with mental health or other needs; level and extent of PRS depends on needs and appropriations. ORR shall not delay release if PRS are not immediately available.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS service area — placement stability and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall work with sponsors to address parenting and caring challenges, including guidance about maintaining a safe home, supervision, protecting from smugglers/traffickers/gangs, and information about child abuse, neglect, separation, grief and loss and their effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS service area — immigration proceedings assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall help facilitate the sponsor's plan to ensure the child's attendance at all immigration court proceedings and compliance with DHS requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS service area — guardianship information
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sponsor is not a parent or legal guardian, PRS providers shall provide information about the benefits of obtaining legal guardianship and may assist in identifying legal resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS service area — legal services assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall assist sponsors in accessing relevant legal service resources including immigration matters and unresolved juvenile justice issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS service area — education assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall assist with school enrollment, addressing school progress and attendance issues, and alternative education plans for children who exceed mandatory school age; they may assist sponsors with obtaining evaluations for suspected disabilities to determine eligibility for special education or reasonable modifications and auxiliary aids/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS service area — employment education (child labor laws)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall educate sponsors on U.S. child labor laws and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS service area — medical services assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall assist sponsors in obtaining medical insurance if available, locating medical providers to meet individual needs, assist with making and keeping appointments for specialized medical assistance, and provide referrals and information relevant to health considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS service area — individual mental health services
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall provide sponsors with relevant mental health resources and referrals for the child and assist with making and keeping mental health appointments and monitoring mental health requirements when specialized assistance is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources/referrals shall take into account individual needs of child and sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS service area — family stabilization and counseling
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall provide sponsors with relevant resources and referrals for family counseling and/or individual counseling that meet individual needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS service area — substance use resources
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall assist the sponsor in locating resources to address any substance use-related needs of the child.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS service area — gang prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall provide the sponsor information about gang prevention programs in the sponsor's community.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS service area — other specialized services
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers may assist sponsor and child with accessing local resources in other specialized service areas based on needs and at the request of the child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional PRS referral categories (children requiring additional consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional children may be referred to PRS based on needs, including unaccompanied children in need of particular services/treatment, children with disabilities, LGBTQI+ children, adjudicated delinquent or high-risk for juvenile justice involvement, children separated from parent/legal guardian by DHS, victims of human trafficking or other crimes, victims of or at risk for worker exploitation or labor trafficking, certain parolees, and children chronically absent or retained in school.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS assessments — content and approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRS provider shall assess the released child and sponsor for PRS needs and shall document the assessment; the assessment shall be developmentally appropriate, trauma-informed, and focused on needs of the child and sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing check-ins and in-home visits requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall determine appropriate methods, timeframes, and schedule for ongoing contact with the released child and sponsor based on level of need; they shall make monthly contact at a minimum, either in person or virtually, for six months after release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers shall document all ongoing check-ins and in-home visits, and document progress and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS referrals to community resources and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall work with released children and sponsors to access community resources and shall document any community resource referrals and their outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframes to start PRS
rubrics_metrics.description: For children required under TVPRA to receive PRS, providers shall to the greatest extent practicable start services within two days of release; if unable, start no later than 30 days after release. For referred children not required to receive PRS following a home study, start services within two days of accepting a referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination/length of PRS
rubrics_metrics.description: For required PRS under TVPRA, PRS shall continue until the child turns 18 or the child is granted voluntary departure, immigration status, or an order of removal. For non-required but authorized PRS, services presumptively continue for not less than six months or until the child turns 18, or until the provider assesses PRS are no longer needed (but at least six months).

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS records and reporting — case file maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall maintain comprehensive, accurate, and current case files on children that are kept confidential and secure at all times and shall be accessible to ORR upon request; case file information must be kept together in the provider's physical and electronic files.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS documentation upload timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall upload all PRS documentation on services provided to children and sponsors to ORR's case management system within seven days of completion of the services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records management and retention policies
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall have written policies/procedures for organizing and maintaining active and closed case files, including preventing physical damage/destruction; providers must have administrative and physical controls to prevent unauthorized access, may not release records to third parties without ORR approval, and must provide all active and closed case file records to ORR if they no longer provide PRS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and information-sharing controls
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall have written policies/procedures protecting sensitive information of released children from unauthorized users, shall explain to children and sponsors how/when/under what circumstances sensitive information may be shared, and shall have appropriate controls on information-sharing within the provider network including subcontractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Concern (NOC) reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PRS provider is concerned about a child's safety and well-being, the provider shall document a Notification of Concern and report the concerns to ORR and, as applicable, appropriate investigative agencies (including law enforcement and child protective services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers shall document and submit NOCs to ORR within 24 hours of first suspicion or knowledge of the events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case closure procedures for PRS
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers shall formally close a case when ORR terminates PRS in accordance with the termination rules; ORR shall provide appropriate instructions and any relevant forms the providers must follow when closing a case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standards — licensure of standard programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs shall be licensed by an appropriate State or Federal agency, or meet other requirements specified by ORR if licensure is unavailable in the State, to provide residential, group, or foster care services for dependent children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standards — compliance with state and local laws and codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs shall comply with all applicable State child welfare laws and regulations and all State and local building, fire, health, and safety codes, or other ORR-specified requirements if licensure is unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a potential conflict exists between ORR regulations and State law, ORR will review circumstances to determine how to ensure statutory responsibilities; ORR employees must abide by Federal duties if conflict concerns their duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum services — proper physical care and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must provide or arrange for proper physical care and maintenance, including suitable living accommodations and food that is of adequate variety, quality, and in sufficient quantity to supply nutrients needed for proper growth and development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement may be accomplished by following applicable U.S. standards (text cut off in chunk).
